history.hypothesis: The test only waits a fixed 3s then Thread.stop()s the operator, while TestWindowGenerator opens windows only after >1000ms of sweep progress, so delaying sweep() past that deadline stops the thread before any tuple is collected and the size>0 assert fails.

diagnosis.root_cause: emitTestHelper starts InputNode on a background thread, sleeps a fixed 3000ms, then Thread.stop()s it and asserts the sink collected at least one tuple. Emission depends on TestWindowGenerator.sweep() advancing its state machine, and a BEGIN_WINDOW is produced only after wall-clock time has moved more than 1000ms since lastTime. Delaying sweep() by 5000ms (or otherwise starving that thread) means stop() runs before any tuple is delivered, so collectedTuples stays empty and the size>0 assert fails.

evidence.why: The operator is given only a fixed 3s of wall clock before it is forcibly stopped, and the failure stack is this exact assert when the sink is still empty.

Tuples are produced only by sweep() progressing this clock-gated state machine. A 5000ms delay inside sweep exceeds the test's 3000ms deadline, so the thread is stopped before a window tuple is returned and nothing reaches the sink.

diagnosis.root_cause: primitiveBytes asserts that PrimitiveBytes.iterations equals the default trial count (100) after running the nested property via testResult. iterations and values are static and never reset, so a second execution in the same JVM adds another 100 trials to the leftover count and the assertion sees 200.

evidence.why: Failure stack line 119 is this assertEquals. expected:<100> but was:<200> means the property run succeeded but the static counter was already 100 from the previous execution and grew by another full trial count.

iterations is a JVM-lifetime static incremented once per trial and values is a static list that only appends. Nothing clears them between calls to testResult(PrimitiveBytes.class), so the test is not idempotent: one run leaves iterations at 100 and the next run fails with 200. T1 (one run) passes; T2 subrun 1 fails.

evidence.why: Failure stack line 45: expected 100 but was 200. The check assumes iterations equals one property run's trial count, which is only true on the first execution in the JVM.
